ledger.note: 1234: Niebla is independent again. The third period runs 'from 1234 to 1262'; the infobox's Almohad rule ends in 1234. The page names no ruler. Ibn Hud held 'most of al-Andalus' from 1228 (see the Murcia dossier), so the previous holder may have been his state rather than the Almohads; the page is silent. Reviewer eu-12-g (2026-10-25): confidence lowered from 3 to 2: the counterpart conflicts with the Ibn Hud page ('allowing Ibn Hud to seize most of al-Andalus relatively unopposed', 1228) and with the Almohad (af-02) dossier, whose ledger has the Almohads lose the rest of their Iberian land to Ibn Hud in October 1228.

notes: Cliopatria rows: the 1015-1017 shape precedes the page's 1023; the row has no shape for 1018-1027, 1056-1146, 1152-1235 (Seville, the Almoravids and the Almohads held it, per the infobox) and ends in 1249, thirteen years before the conquest of 1262. All five shapes are one ~1,400 km2 outline in Huelva province 22-35 km north of the town of Niebla, which the outline does not contain; a circle round Niebla was added, but neither page gives a boundary or an area (the infobox has none), so the true extent (Huelva? Saltés? Gibraleón? the Aljarafe?) is open. Not settled (page silent): the founding dynasty; the third taifa's ruler and its relation to Castile between 1248 and 1262 (tributary or not); the dates of the shape changes in 1241; the Seville conquest of the neighbour Saltés and Huelva (1051, per that page) against Niebla's 1053. The Alfonso X page was opened and is silent. Mirrors needed: Seville (gain 1053), almoravid-dynasty (loss 1145), almohad-caliphate (gain 1150, loss 1234), crown-of-castile (gain 1262; vassal_start if any). Gazetteer names needed: Niebla (place, Huelva province, 37.355 N 6.68 W), Tejada.
